source_fields.formulation: A fixed sequence of bounded reward distributions may vary over time, and the learner observes only the selected arm's reward. One algorithm must adapt to every undisclosed budget; performance is evaluated using the actual environment's variance and mean variation. Different levels of budget knowledge cannot be interchanged.
source_fields.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.

source_fields.instance: There are $K\ge2$ arms. The reward laws $\nu_{t,i}$ are fixed before interaction, supported on $[0,1]$, and sampled independently across rounds. Denote means by $\mu_{t,i}=\mathbb E X_{t,i}$ and their vector by $\mu_t$. $$V_\mu=\sum_{t=2}^{T}\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty,\qquad Q_{\mathrm{env}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\max_{1\le i\le K}\operatorname{Var}(X_{t,i})\le\frac T4.$$ The quantity $Q_{\mathrm{env}}$ sums the largest arm variance in each round; it is neither the variance sum along the chosen arms nor the sum over all arms.

operations.query_signature: Choose arm $I_t$ and observe one reward $X_{t,I_t}$. Noise may be heteroscedastic or zero, and reward laws may change even when means are constant. Inputs $K,T$ are public; armwise variances, means, change locations, and both budgets $Q,V$ are hidden. A causal policy cannot use undisclosed budgets and must work simultaneously across all such budget classes. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

source_fields.complete_expression: The criterion is expected dynamic pseudo-regret, averaging over rewards and algorithm randomness. Adaptation to an unknown budget uses one algorithm evaluated after the run at the realized budget; it cannot be replaced retrospectively by a budget-aware policy.
